transcript.text:
You are playing BLINDBOARD, a deduction game about a hidden keyboard.

THE BOARD
The board is a one-handed keyboard with 12 keys: 4 fingers (pinky, ring, middle, index) x 3 rows (top, home, bottom). Each key is addressed by finger and row. The complete list of valid key addresses:
L-pinky-top, L-pinky-home, L-pinky-bottom, L-ring-top, L-ring-home, L-ring-bottom, L-middle-top, L-middle-home, L-middle-bottom, L-index-top, L-index-home, L-index-bottom

The 12 symbols A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L are assigned to the 12 keys in a hidden arrangement (each symbol on exactly one key). Your job: work out which symbol is on which key.

EACH TURN
- You press exactly 3 DIFFERENT keys (a chord) by giving their addresses.
- Next turn you are told which 3 symbols those keys held, as an ALPHABETICALLY SORTED list. You are NOT told which symbol came from which key. Overlap your chords cleverly to pin symbols to keys.

ROTATIONS
Pressing disturbs the board: after each of your chords, the keys you just pressed are rotated among themselves — each of those keys ends up with a different one of those same letters. No other keys ever move. Your results always describe the keys as they were BEFORE that rotation.

LOCKS (optional, side score)
On any press turn you may lock letters onto keys you are sure of: +1 point if correct at that moment, -3 if wrong. You get no feedback on locks during the game. Each key can be locked only once, ever.

FINAL GUESS
You may end the game at any time by submitting your full guess. After turn 20 you MUST submit it. Your main score is how many of the 12 keys you guess correctly, judged against the arrangement at the moment you guess.

RESPONSE FORMAT
Reply with ONLY one JSON object, no other text.
To press: {"presses": ["L-pinky-top", "L-ring-home", "L-middle-bottom"]}
To press and lock: {"presses": [ ... 3 addresses ... ], "locks": {"L-pinky-home": "A"}}
To guess (ends the game): {"guess": {"L-pinky-top": "A", ... one entry for every key ...}}
